title: Quantitative Paley-Zygmund Inequality
description: The quantitative Paley-Zygmund inequality with threshold parameter θ: P[X > θE[X]] ≥ (1-θ)²E[X]²/E[X²]

overview.historicalContext: R.E.A.C. Paley and A. Zygmund proved this inequality in 1932 as a tool for establishing lower bounds on the probability that a random variable exceeds a fraction of its mean. While the qualitative version (X > 0 with positive probability when E[X] > 0) is a simple consequence, the quantitative version with threshold parameter θ provides explicit lower bounds. It is a fundamental tool in the probabilistic method for combinatorics (Alon-Spencer, Chapter 4).
overview.problemStatement:
**Quantitative Paley-Zygmund Inequality**:

For a non-negative random variable $X$ with $E[X] > 0$ and $0 \leq \theta < 1$:

$$P[X > \theta \cdot E[X]] \geq (1 - \theta)^2 \cdot \frac{E[X]^2}{E[X^2]}$$

In counting form over a Finset $s$ with non-negative $f$:

$$(1-\theta)^2 (\sum f)^2 \leq |\{a \in s : f(a) > \theta \cdot \mu\}| \cdot \sum f^2$$
overview.text: The quantitative Paley-Zygmund inequality provides a lower bound on the probability that a non-negative random variable exceeds any fraction θ of its mean
overview.proofStrategy:
The proof proceeds by:
1. **Sum decomposition**: Split $\sum f = \sum_{\text{above}} f + \sum_{\text{below}} f$ where 'above' = $\{a : f(a) > \theta \mu\}$
2. **Below-threshold bound**: $\sum_{\text{below}} f \leq \theta \cdot \sum f$ (each term ≤ θμ, and $|\text{below}| \leq |s|$)
3. **Above-threshold bound**: $(1-\theta) \sum f \leq \sum_{\text{above}} f$ (from steps 1-2)
4. **Cauchy-Schwarz on above**: $(\sum_{\text{above}} f)^2 \leq |\text{above}| \cdot \sum_{\text{above}} f^2$
5. **Subset monotonicity**: $\sum_{\text{above}} f^2 \leq \sum_s f^2$
6. **Combine**: $(1-\theta)^2 (\sum f)^2 \leq |\text{above}| \cdot \sum f^2$
keyInsights: The proof uses a discrete Cauchy-Schwarz inequality (sq_sum_le) on the above-threshold subset, which is proved by induction with nlinarith handling the algebraic manipulation.
The sum decomposition Finset.sum_filter_add_sum_filter_not splits the finite sum into above/below-threshold parts cleanly in Lean 4.
At θ=0, the result reduces to (∑f)² ≤ |{f>0}| · ∑f², which is strictly stronger than the qualitative P[X>0] > 0 from ProbMethodSecondMoment.lean.
The counting form avoids division and works over ℚ directly, while the probability form requires dividing by ∑f² > 0.

sections.title: Module Header
sections.summary: Documentation of the quantitative Paley-Zygmund inequality, imports from Mathlib and the parent ProbMethodSecondMoment module.
sections.mathContext: Extends ProbMethodSecondMoment.lean with the threshold-parameter version of the Paley-Zygmund inequality.

sections.title: Discrete Cauchy-Schwarz Lemma
sections.summary: Private lemma sq_sum_le: (∑ f)² ≤ |s| · ∑ f² for finite sums, proved by induction with nlinarith.
sections.mathContext: This is the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for finite sums in the form $(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i)^2 \leq n \sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2$. The inductive proof expands the sum-of-squares of differences $\sum (f(a) - f(b))^2 \geq 0$ and uses nlinarith for the algebraic verification.

sections.title: Quantitative Paley-Zygmund (Counting Form)
sections.summary: The main theorem paley_zygmund_quantitative: (1-θ)²(∑f)² ≤ |above|·∑f² where above = {a : f(a) > θ·μ}. Six-step proof via sum decomposition, Cauchy-Schwarz, and subset monotonicity.
sections.mathContext: The proof combines: (1) sum decomposition via Finset.sum_filter_add_sum_filter_not, (2) below-threshold bound via Finset.sum_le_sum, (3) above-threshold lower bound by subtraction, (4) Cauchy-Schwarz on the above set, (5) subset monotonicity of sum of squares, (6) squaring the lower bound via sq_le_sq'.

sections.title: Probability Form Corollary
sections.summary: Corollary paley_zygmund_probability: (1-θ)²(∑f)²/∑f² ≤ |above|, the fraction form obtained by dividing by ∑f² > 0.
sections.mathContext: This is the standard textbook form of the Paley-Zygmund inequality, where dividing by |s| gives the probability P[X > θE[X]] ≥ (1-θ)²E[X]²/E[X²].

sections.title: θ=0 Specialization
sections.summary: Theorem paley_zygmund_at_zero: at θ=0, reduces to (∑f)² ≤ |{f>0}|·∑f², strengthening the qualitative version.
sections.mathContext: Setting θ=0 eliminates the (1-θ)² factor and the threshold simplifies to f(a) > 0. This gives a quantitative lower bound on the count of positive elements, strictly stronger than just knowing P[X>0] > 0.

crossReferences.description: Extends the qualitative Paley-Zygmund inequality from ProbMethodSecondMoment.lean with a threshold parameter θ, providing quantitative lower bounds.

conclusion.summary: A complete formalization of the quantitative Paley-Zygmund inequality with threshold parameter θ over finite sets. Three theorems (counting form, probability form, θ=0 specialization), 0 sorries, 0 axioms. The proof uses sum decomposition, Cauchy-Schwarz, and subset monotonicity.
conclusion.implications: **Theoretical Significance**: The quantitative Paley-Zygmund inequality is the main tool for lower-tail bounds in the probabilistic method. While the qualitative version only guarantees P[X > 0] > 0, the quantitative version gives explicit concentration bounds. The θ=0 case already strengthens the qualitative result by providing a numerical lower bound on the count of positive elements.
openQuestions: Can the equality characterization be formalized: when does equality hold in Paley-Zygmund (constant f on the above-threshold set)?
Can the Paley-Zygmund inequality be extended to the measure-theoretic setting with Lebesgue integrals?
